programme: FOXP3-driven regulatory T cell (Treg) identity and effector programme, running through its own bound target genes IL2RA, CTLA4, TNFRSF18, IKZF2, GATA3, and FASLG — the canonical FOXP3 Treg gene set.
role_in_a: In glioblastoma, FOXP3+ Tregs infiltrate the tumor microenvironment and suppress anti-tumor immunity, contributing to immune evasion and resistance to checkpoint blockade and chemo-radiotherapy; direct primary evidence spans immunotherapy trials, metabolic reprogramming of Tregs, spatial immune profiling of tumor core vs. periphery, and intervention studies showing FOXP3 blockade restores treatment response.
role_in_b: In stroke, FOXP3+ Tregs are recruited to the injured brain where they dampen neuroinflammation, limit secondary tissue damage, and support functional recovery; primary evidence covers Treg involvement in synaptic/motor recovery after focal brain injury, Treg-mediated limitation of deficits after CNS trauma, and a pharmacological Treg-induction axis (RUNX1/CBFβ/FOXP3) in an ischemia-relevant model.
shared_axis: Both diseases place a CNS lesion (tumor or infarct) under local immune control by FOXP3+ Tregs, but with opposite consequence: in glioblastoma Treg activity is pathogenic, suppressing tumor clearance, while in stroke Treg activity is protective, suppressing secondary neuroinflammation. The same differentiation/effector module is co-opted in both settings because CNS lesions of very different origin both generate a local antigen/damage signal that recruits and depends on Treg biology.
reasoning: FOXP3 clears a high, non-single-group recurrence bar (13/24) and the record independently places it with primary, disease-specific papers in both glioblastoma and stroke, plus two entries the retrieval marks as spanning both — enough to name and place the module without inventing biology, but no single source states that these two diseases share this axis, so the connection rests on each disease's separately established Treg literature rather than a documented joint claim.
support: PMID 42043781 — immune checkpoint/PI3K-AKT trial data implicating Treg-relevant pathway in glioblastoma; PMID 42649887 — Treg-mediated immune resistance via fatty acid metabolism in glioblastoma; PMID 40996683 — spatial distribution of tumor-infiltrating immune cells (glioblastoma); PMID 40582634 — direct FOXP3 blockade in glioblastoma boosts chemo-radiotherapy response; PMID 42642017 — synaptic plasticity/motor recovery after focal brain injury (stroke-side FOXP3 placement); PMID 40478534 — Treg role limiting visual deficits after CNS trauma; PMID 41201767 — RUNX1/CBFβ/FOXP3 axis driving Treg accumulation in an ischemia-relevant model; PMID 25555571 and PMID 35345443 — flagged by the record as concerning both diseases, linking FOXP3+ Treg proportions/expression to tumor and gut-brain-axis contexts respectively, though their titles read primarily glioma-focused and should be read directly before leaning on them further.
how_to_falsify: Deplete FOXP3+ Tregs (anti-CD25 or FOXP3-DTR ablation) in matched glioblastoma and ischemic-stroke mouse models: the account predicts tumor growth/immune evasion should fall in the glioblastoma model while infarct volume and neuroinflammatory damage should rise in the stroke model. If depletion moves both models in the same direction, or has no effect in one, the shared-but-opposite-valence Treg module account is wrong. A complementary check is CUT&RUN for FOXP3 at IL2RA/CTLA4/TNFRSF18 in Tregs isolated from tumor-infiltrating vs. peri-infarct tissue to confirm the same target program is actually engaged in both settings.
caveats: Blood|brain tissue pairing with only 24 patient-group comparisons drawn from 4 independent cohort pairs — a modest base. The exclusion list removed several classic immune/vascular master regulators (NOTCH1, ERG, BCL6, NFATC1, NFATC2, NR3C2, CREB5, HLX, LITAF, CEBPD, SREBF2, PBX1) as tissue-generic, which means generic blood/brain immune or vascular infiltration signal is already stripped out — FOXP3's survival and disease-specific opposing-direction literature is what distinguishes it from that generic background, but the margin (13/24) is not overwhelming. Other concordant factors in this list (ISL1, MEIS1, SOX17, NR2F2, PRDM16, FOXN1, ZNF281, TCFL5, GTF3A, ZNF354C, POU4F2) carry separate biology — developmental-reprogramming and vascular-identity signals — that does not fold into the Treg programme and was deliberately not forced into this account; none of the single-view factors (LITAF, TRRAP, CEBPD, HDAC9, SOX6, KMT2E, SMARCC1) were used.
